config.title: Berlin Mugs - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which Berlin mug to give, what the Christmas market deposit means and where my mugs ship.

items.q: What is the best Berlin mug to give as a gift?
items.a: Match the mug to the person. **Ampelmann** for kids, the **Starbucks** city mug only for someone who collects them, **KPM** porcelain for parents or a wedding, and a mug that shows a real Berlin place they know for friends and colleagues. I would skip the mug that only says BERLIN in big letters.

items.q: Can you keep the mug from a Berlin Christmas market?
items.a: Yes. You pay a **deposit (Pfand)** of a few euros on top of the drink. Give the mug back and you get the deposit back, keep it and the deposit is what you paid for it. Many markets print their name and the year on the mug.

items.q: Where can I buy a Starbucks Berlin mug?
items.a: Starbucks sells its **city mugs** in its stores rather than online, so ask in a Berlin store which Berlin design is current. Older ones turn up with collectors and resellers. It is the right gift for someone who collects those mugs from every city they visit.

items.q: How big is a standard coffee mug?
items.a: A normal coffee mug holds about **300 to 350 ml**. My Berlin mugs hold **325 ml**, which is about 11 US fluid ounces.

items.q: Do your Berlin mugs ship outside Germany?
items.a: Yes. They are **made to order**, and shipping is **free to Germany, the UK and the US**, with **€4.90** to the rest of the EU. So you can send one straight to family or friends abroad.
